subject: botany_2
question_text: The proportion of nucleotides in a nucleic acid is: adenine 18%, guanine 30%, cytosine 42%, uracil 10%. Name the nucleic acid and state the number of strands.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.44, printed question 105. insider_note: Two clues, two answers. Uracil names the molecule; the failed pairing rule names the strand count.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Which nucleic acid
steps.margin_note: Name the clue, then the answer. Three lines.
lines: URACIL is present, and thymine is absent.
So the nucleic acid is RNA.
steps.why: Uracil is the one base that appears in RNA and never in DNA, so its presence settles the question by itself.
common_mistakes: Answering DNA. DNA contains thymine, never uracil.
Not saying why. Name the clue — uracil is present and thymine is absent — as well as the answer.
